name: POST /api/users/{id}/activate - Open an account for use
description: Sets is_active true, stamps activated_at on the first activation and clears any closure stamps, so the same endpoint completes an invitation and reopens an account that was closed by mistake. Proves criterion 4c12f924-87d1-4be1-b790-d94a936d58b3#AC1 by making an invitation redeemable without touching the database. 200 rather than 201: it is an action on an existing resource. Governed on user.deactivate, deliberately the SAME grant as closure - the authority is 'decides whether this person may sign in', and a model where closing needs a grant that reopening does not is a model where a mistake cannot be undone by the person who made it. The optional initial_password is the only way a person invited here can sign in at all, because LeadFlow has no mail transport and there is no self-service link to send; it is refused with 501 once ProjexCloud is the identity authority, which is the same handover guard that turns off local register and login. The response states credential_issued rather than implying access was granted; the password itself never reaches the audit metadata, only the fact that one was issued. QA: reactivates the account closed by POST /api/users/{id}/deactivate, which is why it runs after it; requiresRole admin, so no Authorization header is declared here (MUST-71).

testCases.name: Reopen the closed account and issue its initial credential
NEGATIVE: an initial password shorter than twelve characters
NEGATIVE: no Authorization header at all

errorCases.when: initial_password is present but shorter than twelve characters, or is not a string
the Authorization header is absent, or present without a bearer token

an initial_password was supplied while a ProjexCloud identity issuer is configured. Writing a local hash would create the second credential store that AuthService.assertLocalCredentialsPermitted exists to prevent - two stores that both answer 'yes' is how a revoked user keeps working.
errorCases._whyNotReproducible: It is a DEPLOYMENT state, not a request: reproducing it means configuring PROJEXCLOUD_IDENTITY_ISSUER_URL on the server under test, which would simultaneously turn off POST /api/auth/register and POST /api/auth/login and take the entire suite's auth producer with it.

errorCases.when: no user on the register holds that id
errorCases._whyNotReproducible: MUST-36 bans a generated id in a path parameter and there is no producer for an id that provably matches no row.

errorCases.when: the caller does not hold user.deactivate
errorCases._whyNotReproducible: MUST-64/MUST-71: it needs a token from a different role, and this definition declares requiresRole so the runner pre-fetches the admin identity.
